system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid military and diplomatic escalation centered on Yemen’s Houthi movement is reshaping regional security: cross-border strikes on Saudi facilities, Yemeni offensives to retake territory, and plans to break Houthi control of Red Sea choke points. External actors (Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the US) are adjusting military aid, basing and legal postures, producing interactive feedbacks between combat operations, maritime security, and diplomatic/legal constraints. As an open system this involves multiple actors, material flows (weapons, shipping, energy), and political-legal feedback loops that can amplify escalation or open pathways for containment.
system_description.scope: Inside: Houthi movement, Yemeni government/armed forces, Saudi military operations, Iran's regional proxies and influence, Egypt and US military/diplomatic actions; processes of offensive/defensive operations, missile/drone strikes on energy infrastructure, maritime interdiction at Bab el-Mandeb/Red Sea, legal and basing disputes (e.g., use of overseas bases), and consequences for shipping and energy flows.
system_description.super_system: Middle East regional security and global energy/maritime governance, embedded in broader Iran-driven regional conflict dynamics and great-power competition.
adjacent_subsystems: Global maritime trade & energy supply chains
International law, basing arrangements & military aid diplomacy
evidence_headlines: Yemeni government launches offensive to seize all areas from Iran-backed Houthis
Houthis claim strike on Saudi Aramco facility as Yemen fighting intensifies
Yemen's Houthis say they attacked Aramco facility in Riyadh with missiles, drones
Saudis plan assault on Houthis to break Red Sea chokehold
Yemeni government forces drive Houthis from Bab el-Mandeb Strait
EXCLUSIVE: Citing Iran war, US waives rights condition on Egypt military aid - reuters.com

variables.name: Non-state armed group offensive capability
variables.description: The aggregate combat power, reach and strike-readiness of non-state armed actors operating in the theatre.

variables.name: State military defensive capacity
variables.description: The ability of state-aligned forces to detect, deter and absorb attacks and to defend territory and critical infrastructure.

variables.name: Cross-border attack rate
variables.description: The frequency at which kinetic or remote-attack operations cross international boundaries per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime chokepoint control
variables.description: The degree to which any actor or coalition exerts effective control or denial over strategic sea lanes and straits.

variables.name: External support flow to local actors
variables.description: The rate of transfer of materiel, funding, intelligence and advisory support from outside actors to local forces.

variables.name: Regional naval presence density
variables.description: The concentration of naval and maritime security assets operating in and near key sea lanes and littoral zones.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: The susceptibility of energy production, processing and transport assets to disruption or damage from attacks or spillovers.

variables.name: Shipping reroute rate
variables.description: The proportion or volume of commercial maritime traffic diverting from primary routes to avoid perceived risks per unit time.

variables.name: Legal and basing restrictions
variables.description: The degree of legal, diplomatic and host-state constraints on the use of foreign bases and overflight/operational rights.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The level and frequency of formal diplomatic interactions, negotiations and crisis-management efforts among relevant actors.

variables.name: Escalation pressure
variables.description: The net systemic tendency toward intensification of conflict, reflecting accumulating triggers, grievances and incentives to escalate.

variables.name: External patron influence
variables.description: The political and operational leverage that external patrons exert over local actors' strategic decisions and alignments.

variables.name: Arms flow volume
variables.description: The quantity and tempo of weapons, munitions and delivery systems entering the conflict environment per unit time.

variables.name: Global energy price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability in global energy prices that affects economic and political responses to disruptions.

variables.name: Maritime interdiction rate
variables.description: The frequency of interdiction, boarding, seizure or attack events against commercial vessels in the region per unit time.

variables.name: Perception of legality of military actions
variables.description: The prevailing international and domestic judgments about the legality and legitimacy of military operations and their political acceptability.

catalysts.title: Yemeni government territorial offensive
catalysts.description: Ongoing offensive by Yemeni government forces to seize Houthi-held areas, likely to continue operations to retake territory.

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi strikes on Saudi energy and territory
catalysts.description: Houthis have escalated long-range strikes against Saudi facilities and territory and are likely to continue external attacks.

catalysts.title: Contest for Bab el-Mandeb Strait control

catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Portugal prosecutors probe legality of US use of Lajes base in Iran war'.
